entry.text: (и снова какое-то интро.... ето ппц я вообще хз как начинать каждый день.....)
(Oh that's Erika.)
(Sweet girl powered by hyperfixations and the ability to find childlike wonder in the most boring trash imaginable.)
(Probably the only one who gave a shit about me before I left.)
Gail! Oh my god, it really is you.
I totally thought you'd leave Larris again right after the funeral. Like poof - stormy beach, dramatic coat, no forwarding address.
But then Father Jean-Noël said he saw you in here, and I thought he was joking. But look at that. You didn't leave.
I still have to deal with the flat. Paperwork, dust, old things. After that I can...

options.text: Sell it and leave the town

response.text: (Here comes that soft disappointed look. I deserve it.)
Oh. Right. Makes sense, I guess.
Well, then I'll just enjoy it while it lasts.

options.text: Try fixing it up and stay here

response.text: Really? That's... kind of nice. I mean, it'd be nice. If you did.

entry.text: But since when are you a cashier? I always pictured you ending up in a lighthouse, or something like that. Hallucinating mermaids and fighting with gulls and stuff.

response.text: Uh oh, smells like denial in here.
Yeah... Félix happened, I suppose.
That's my girl.

entry.text: Well, point is - I'm glad you're back.

wby.text: Hmm... well, I finished school last year. Now I write little pieces for the paper - whatever happens in Larris, basically.
Plus I sometimes send spooky stories to one underground magazine in Montpensier.
Oh, and I got a scooter. Finally. It's silly, but I love it.
...I think about leaving too, sometimes. Traveling. Maybe doing real journalism. But... I guess I'm not as brave as you were.
(That's cute how she thinks it was about being brave rather than running away.)

seals.text: Yeah... My sweet big floppers. White puffballs, speckled blobs, silly whiskery noses - I love every single version.
You know, they showed up a bit early this year, and on such odd night.
First seal appeared, all round and confused. Full moon overhead. And a few hours later - boom. Our sad little organ falls apart.
...By the way. Do you know who's helping out at the church these days?
No? Jean-Noël doesn't handle it all himself anymore?
Oh, I'll let you find out. It's more fun that way.

end.text: So... Did you want to buy something, or...?
Oh, no no, I just wanted to see you before work.
I'll come bug you again later! Take care, okay?

after.text: There's something on the floor. Looks like a torn-out notebook paper with some pattern.
(Of course Erika dropped it. Some things never change.)
(I'll take a look when it's quiet.)

entry.text: Good morning. What a beautiful day it is today.
No parcels or letters for this address. Just here for the blue Jesuses and three toffies, please.

entry_decor_ordered.text: Good morning. What a beautiful day it is today.
I've got a parcel for the shop. Could you sign here?
Thanks. And I'll take the blue Jesuses and three toffies, please.

response.text: And you're already back in town, aren't you?
...Of course I'm back. A little "mild head injury and mud exposure" won't stop me or my bike.
Glad you understand.

options.text: I'd just lie in a ditch forever

response.text: Yeah, I used to feel like that. Then one day I decided I was a cat, and God gave me nine lives.
Oh, blue JC. Jesus Christ, a lot of people call them that. You know what those letters actually stand for?

options.text: Probably Jean-Claude or some other name

response.text: Okay. Sounds legit.
I like this version too.
Come on, they're not that bad.

bell.text: Lost the bell again, though. Shame. I liked that one.

wrong_items_jesuses.text: JC. Blue packet. And three toffee candies. Wrapper with cow spots.

checkout.text: Thanks. Back to work. Would be nice not to meet the pavement today.

after_decor_ordered.text: (Alright, mystery parcel. Let's see what's inside.)

options.text: Looks like it came out of a bin
Oh joy, long live bad taste
Ugly enough to feel like home

entry.text: (Ah, yes. Shared lice, first cigarettes and years of mutual embarrassment.)
(That special kind of friend you've known long enough to forget how it started, and way too long to come out of it clean. Nostalgia with a side of nausea.)
(Let's call him...)

response.text: Hey. Yeah, I heard you were back.
Came to say hi to your dear old friend?
I'm here to buy Jean-Noël his mugwort Fleuries. That's all.
What, still haven't learned to form a thought?
No, I didn't end up in jail like you all expected. Yeah, that's a rosary you're staring at. Cool one. Not some dainty shit, obviously.
...Jean-Noël asked me to pick up his mugwort Fleuries. That's all.

click.text: Funny seeing you behind a counter selling cigs. Thought you'd still be nicking 'em.

response.text: Huh. Not in a padded room, then?
Good start. Still a little bitch, I see.

options.text: Do I see a rosary bracelet?

response.text: Yeah. Cool one. Heavy beads, solid grip. Church-approved stress ball, as Jean-Noël says.

options.text: So you hang out with the church now?

response.text: *sigh*
...As you probably remember, a couple of years ago the cops stuck me with church crap for community service. Thought I'd fake it, punch a few pews and be done.
Then... things got weird. Decked some junkie who pissed on the altar. Crashed in one of the graves I'd just dug. Woke up to chase looters outta the cemetery.
...Time passed. My hours were up.
I just... stayed.
Doesn't matter.

options.text: Heard the nuns think you wrecked the organ

response.text: Oh, of course they'd think it was me. Everyone thinks that.
(God's angriest little helper.)
Yeah, sure. Blame the walking fuck-up. Wouldn't be the worst thing I've done, right?
Jesus. You really don't think people can get better?
They can. Rare, though.
You know what? Fuck this. Believe whatever you want.
I'm leaving today. Do me a favour and be gone again when I get back.
Doesn't help to repeat it. Just give me the damn cigs.
Smoking fucking quit ME. Real men breathe air and trouble, not that weak shit.
...Also Jean-Noël's hippie-smoke near gave me anaphylaxis.

options.text: So you're a good boy now?

response.text: That's disgusting. But yeah, sort of. Trying to be. At least haven't hated myself as much lately.

options.text: What did your boss ask you to buy?

response.text: Those flowery ones. Mugwort something... Fleuries.

checkout.text: I'm leaving today. Took a shift on a trawler to make some money before the weather turns to shit. Just thought I'd say something before going. Unlike some people.
Not like you'll still be here when I get back, obviously.

after_butthurt.text: Wow. Didn't even take the cigs.

entry.text: Hey, guess what I just saw.
There's a seal. Like, on the pavement, near the soup truck. Just lying there... And it's perfect.
Some of the fishermen saw it first. Said it's not scared. Not hurt. Just... there.
I ran into Eel Lady down at the docks and she said I could take a few fish if I brought her some chewing tobacco. So yeah. This, please.

click.text: Sorry, Gail. Seal first. Gossip later.

response.text: Chewing tobacco. For Eel Lady.

wrong_items.text: Oh, could you also add a couple of newspapers? To wrap the fish. Maybe... three? Better too many than not enough, right?

wrong_items_wrap.text: Chewing tobacco and three newspapers, Gail. If you're forgetting too, we're doomed.

checkout.text: Okay. Fish, tobacco, newspaper. Oh no, the camera. I need a photo for the paper.

entry.text: Hi.

response.text: ...Not even close. Menthol Morleys, please.
...Oh. Yeah, right.
...And you're?..
Okay, Abigaïl. I'm Madeleine, by the way.
Please no. If I hear that name one more time this month, I swear... This town's obsessed.
Mhm. Mom loves them.
Thanks for not saying Mary Magdalene, by the way. I've heard that name more this month than my whole life.
Okay, Gail. I'm Mado, by the way.
...Fish? Alright... I'm Mado. Short for Madeleine.
Please no. If I hear that name one more time this month, I swear... This town's obsessed.
Mhm. Mom loves them.
Thanks for not saying Mary Magdalene, by the way. I've heard that name more this month than my whole life.
...Ehm. Menthol Morleys, please.
...Cool. Menthol Morleys. Please.
Hospital. I'm here for my training year.
(Ha, knew it. Serious face. Loud heels. Of course she's not local.)
Menthol Morleys. Seriously?

entry.text: Good evening, {{name_yves}}. Mind if I hang around a bit? Waiting on Félix.
He said he's got a plan. Which rarely end well, but they're never boring. Even told me to bring the trombone tonight.
Would never miss it.

response.text: So far so good. I mean, it's been half-dead for a decade at least, and all we can really do now is keep frankensteining it together. But no one in this town ever minded its crooked charm. I think it'll be fine.
Saw it. Smart beast. Lies around, gets fed. Does better than most of us.
Maybe there was something weird there?
(If that doodle wasn't just a joke, and the left panel's hiding something... Yves would've found it by now, right?)
Hm... That side was much worse than the rest of the buffet. Pipes knocked out of place, some mold, bit of rot. But nothing too special. Old things fall apart funny sometimes.
...Strange thing to ask.
(Alright. Let's pull that thread.)
Couldn't it have been prevented? I heard bellows are often the first thing to go. Problematic part.
...Most irritating to check.

...Bellows are a pain, yeah. And in case of this particular organ, what was the point anyway? It wasn't only about bellows, the whole left half was a mess. Pipes knocked out of place, some mold, bit of rot. Keyboard too - half the keys loose, a few straight-up gone.
So... yeah. Whole thing was dying already.
And you helped it die faster?

Helped it die? I did every bloody check they asked for, twice a year, reports sent straight to the diocese. Told them it was falling apart and needed proper repairs, not patch jobs and prayers. No reaction. Nothing changed.
Eventually I stopped checking it properly. Just looked at the parts you could see without crawling in all the way. Figured if they didn't care, why should I?

options.text: So you cracked first, like a loser?
All that ass and no squat

response.text: Well. Maybe I could've done my job better.
...I'll take it off the repair cost. Not much, but fair's fair.
You can be really nasty, huh?

entry.text: Evening, sunshines.
Took you long enough.
Time is fake. Anyway, you closing?
Closing sounds good.
Yeah. Closing sounds good.
Perfect. Grab the key. Pretend we're a real business.

dialog.text: Some old faces and one new snout.

start.text: Right. The plan. The plan is simple.
Father Jean-Noël needs a grave dug, but that skinhead church boy is off playing sailor. So I offered to help. Figured I'd bring Yves along to make it feel like a party.
Ah. Manual labor and midnight brass. How can I say no.
And maybe a bottle of church wine if we charm him right. It is Friday, after all.

options.text: Take a look at the seal

response.text: Then follow the sound of Erika's voice. Can't miss it.

options.text: Go bother Erika if I find her

response.text: Then look somewhere near the seal. Can't miss it.
Sooodoku and siiilence, dear. Got your knitting too?
...Jeepers creepers. Easy there.

d2bye_yves_fish.text: Mademoiselle said her name is Fish. As in Félicia.

d2end_outro2seal.text: Gail wandered through the town square, then the park, then down to the docks. She never found the seal, just sky, sea, and gulls. That was enough.

d2end_outro2erika.text: Gail checked Erika's house. Then the back of the post office, where the newspaper team hides. Erika wasn't anywhere, but the Friday buzz of pubs and cafés wasn't too bad either.

d2end_outro2sudoku.text: Sudoku always calmed Gail down, even when her hand filled the numbers almost without thinking.
Her pencil broke near the end. She couldn't find a single sharpener that hadn't been taken apart years ago. But the last few numbers were obvious, anyway.

d2end_outro2dread.text: Gail spent the evening poking old scars, staring at the ceiling, and quietly reconsidering her entire life.
Then she got bored and fell asleep.
